title: Risk-stratification tools for emergency department patients with syncope: A systematic review and meta-analysis of direct evidence for SAEM GRACE
summary: This review included 31 reports evaluating 13 syncope prediction rules. Among repeatedly validated tools, CSRS pooled sensitivity was 89% (95% CI 76–95.4%) and specificity 48.1% (34.5–61.9%), with substantial heterogeneity. No randomized comparison with clinician judgment was found; the single direct observational comparison included 488 patients.
findings: SFSR had 12 validation studies; CSRS and OESIL each had five.
Comparative certainty was low because of indirectness and suspected publication bias.
Missed serious outcomes and unnecessary admission are competing harms; this review did not test a score-driven disposition intervention.
comparator: Other rules; limited direct comparison with unstructured clinician judgment.
population: ED patients aged at least 16 with syncope or near-syncope; target question concerned patients without a serious diagnosis at initial evaluation.
limitations: Searches ended in June 2023; heterogeneous composites, follow-up and indirect comparisons limit applicability. Subsequent 2026 validation found FAINT more sensitive than physician estimates for cardiac outcomes, so the review's historical conclusion needs that qualification.
intervention: Syncope risk-stratification rules, including CSRS, SFSR and OESIL.
whyItMatters: A score alone cannot establish safe discharge after unexplained syncope. This historical review documents uncertainty about comparative performance, rather than proving clinician judgment superior or scores ineffective.
evidenceNotes: Publisher main methods, results, GRADE tables and limitations reviewed; separate supplements not reviewed. Derivation/validation samples overlap; no artificial unique-patient total is supplied. Bounded DOI correction/retraction searches found no separate notice, without proving absence. Later primary context: https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.17362 (publisher online May 19, 2026): 1,263 patients; FAINT versus physician sensitivity difference 18.7 percentage points (95% CI 6.8–30.6) for cardiac outcomes. Observational validation does not establish implementation benefit. This review is evidence supporting GRACE development, not a new SAEM clinical policy.
primaryEndpoint: Prediction of serious adverse outcomes, chiefly within 30 days; some included studies used longer follow-up.
